correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Laurent-ring T=[[s+s^-1,1],[1,0]] with det one. Its recurrence P_t and determinant s^-t(s^t+1)^2 yield Smith factors (s^t+1,s^t+1) for even t and ((s^t+1)/(s+1),(s^t+1)(s+1)) for odd t. The s=1 root multiplicity contributes exactly the odd/odd single-unit deficiency in kernel dimension. Moebius inversion of fixed counts proves primitive cycles; for odd n the identity T^n=I+[[J,J],[J,J]] yields F^n(z)=z+pi(z)(1,1), and translation by E=(1,0) toggles parity and doubles/halves primitive period. No step extrapolates finite tests to infinite n.
